items.title: India Began Building Bridges When the World Was Building Walls: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal
items.summary: He noted that India recorded USD 863 billion in exports last year and has set itself the target of achieving USD 1 trillion in exports in the current year. This would represent nearly 16 per cent growth in a year when international trade is expected to grow by only around 2.5 to 3 per cent, while the global economy remains vulnerable to shocks and global growth is expected to fall below 3 per cent.

facts.text: He noted that India recorded USD 863 billion in exports last year and has set itself the target of achieving USD 1 trillion in exports in the current year.

This would represent nearly 16 per cent growth in a year when international trade is expected to grow by only around 2.5 to 3 per cent, while the global economy remains vulnerable to shocks and global growth is expected to fall below 3 per cent.

Shri Goyal expressed confidence that India would achieve the USD 1 trillion export target, noting that the target has been set not merely by the government but by the people and businesses of India, including 63 million MSMEs, large and small industries, global capability centres and around 250,0…

He also said that the Reserve Bank of India had once again raised its growth projections for the current year and expressed confidence that India would continue to grow at over 7 per cent and remain the fastest-growing large economy.

facts.text: A key focus of the Roundtable was the implementation of the Telecommunication (Right of Way) Rules, 2024, notified by DoT under the Telecommunications Act, 2023.

The ABP is aimed at upgrading the existing BharatNet network, creating incremental network infrastructure for new Gram Panchayats (GPs), connecting non-GP villages on demand and providing 1.5 crore fibre internet connections.
As of August 2026, 55,780 km of Optical Fibre Cable had been laid and 28,700 Gram Panchayats had been upgraded and connected under ABP.

bullets: TRAI (Telecom Regulatory Authority of India): Basis TRAI Act, 1997; Function Regulator of telecom and broadcasting (tariffs, quality of service, recommendations on spectrum/licensing)

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 19 › Telecom technologies - 3G to 5G and 6G roadmap, satellite communication, optical fibre › Optical fibre - working principle, signal form, undersea cables (CANI), national fibre targets
bullets: Works on total internal reflection; signals travel as pulses of light (LENS Sep 2025). It is the fastest data-transmission medium compared with copper cable, radio waves and satellite signals (APPSC 2025 asked).
Main use is communication; single-mode fibre carries signals over long distances, multi-mode over short runs .

Undersea cables are fibre-optic lines on the seabed, about 1.5 million km globally; optical repeaters every 60-80 km; carry nearly 99% of international internet and telecom traffic; cheaper and lower-latency than satellites (LENS Sep 2025).

National fibre: NOFN planned to link all 2,50,000 Gram Panchayats using existing PSU fibre (BSNL, RailTel, Power Grid); funded by USOF; uses GPON technology; est. cost Rs 20,000 cr (APP). NOFN was later renamed BharatNet .
Exam angle: statement sets on TIR, light signals and single-mode fibre ("All of the above").

bullets: Router: Role Connects different networks, routes by IP; OSI layer Network (3)

Transmission modes: simplex (one way: radio/TV broadcast, keyboard), half duplex (both ways, one at a time: walkie-talkie), full duplex (both at once: telephone) .

Connections: DSL runs on the telephone copper line, cable on coaxial TV cable, fibre on light pulses in optical fibre . Satellite internet has space, ground and user (VSAT) segments and needs no terrestrial wire.

items.title: India Highlights Regional Energy Cooperation and Energy Security at 20th EAS Energy Ministers’ Meeting
items.summary: 08 OCT 2026 1:12PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of State for Power and New & Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, represented India at the 20th East Asia Summit Energy Ministers’ Meeting held in Manila, Philippines, today. Addressing the Meeting, Shri Naik emphasised India’s commitment to strengthening regional energy cooperation, energy security and a secure, resilient, affordable and sustainable energy future.

facts.text: 08 OCT 2026 1:12PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of State for Power and New & Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, represented India at the 20th East Asia Summit Energy Ministers’ Meeting held in Manila, Philippines, today.

He also recalled Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s announcement at the 22nd ASEAN India Summit in 2025 to support the ASEAN Power Grid initiative through training of 400 professionals on grid connectivity.

Shri Naik drew attention to India’s significant progress in the power sector, with installed electricity generation capacity reaching 558.8 GW as on 30 th September, 2026, including 308 GW of non fossil capacity, accounting for 55% of total installed capacity.
He also highlighted the progress under PM Surya Ghar, with approximately 5.01 million rooftop solar installations benefiting 5.95 million households as on September 29, 2026.

items.title: India Targets 10% of Global 6G Patents and Standards: Union Minister of State for Communications Dr Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani
items.summary: He acknowledged the hard work of industry stakeholders in making these achievements possible. Referring to the strengthening of the telecom sector over the last year, Dr Pemmasani stated that most of the rules under the Telecommunications Act, 2023 have now been notified. He said the objective is to create a regulatory framework that is simpler, technology-neutral and suited to the needs of the modern technology era.

facts.text: Referring to the strengthening of the telecom sector over the last year, Dr Pemmasani stated that most of the rules under the Telecommunications Act, 2023 have now been notified.
The Minister of State further said that nearly 136 R&D projects, worth approximately ₹500 crore, have been funded under the Telecom Technology Development Fund (TTDF).
Dr Pemmasani further exhorted close cooperation between government, operators, equipment manufacturers and technology companies.

items.title: NHAI Releases Document on ‘Wildlife Mitigation Measures & Structures’ Highlighting Strengthened Wildlife Conservation Measures Along National Highways
items.summary: The document was recently released by Shri Nitin Gadkari, Hon’ble Minister for Road Transport and Highways during Chintan Shivir held in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat. The document reflects NHAI’s approach towards developing National Highway infrastructure that balances requirements of connectivity and mobility with environmental sustainability and wildlife conservation.

facts.text: Over last five years, around Rs. 19,700 crores have been invested in wildlife mitigation infrastructure and related environmental protection measures across National Highway projects.
NHAI’s mitigation planning is guided by the ecological sensitivity of project corridors, wildlife movement patterns and the technical feasibility of infrastructure design.

As part of the structural mitigation measures, around Rs. 4,600 crores have been invested in animal underpasses, Rs. 650 crores in animal overpasses, Rs. 8,300 crores in viaducts, Rs. 2,800 crores in tunnels, Rs. 2,500 crores in major bridges and Rs. 500 crores in minor bridges.

To guide wildlife towards designated crossing structures and reduce the possibility of animal–vehicle conflicts, guide fencing and noise barriers have been provided at over 300 km of National Highway alignments.

facts.text: 08 OCT 2026 12:52PM by PIB Delhi The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Fazilka city and adjoining areas (in Punjab LSA) , during the month of August 2026, for information of general telecom consumers.

TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests including City drive – 184.6 KMs, Walk test-1.9 KMs & Hotspot locations - 06 across Fazilka city and adjoining areas during 5 th August to 7 th August 2026 in Punjab LSA.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-1 › Services sector - growth, composition and contribution to GDP and employment › Services exports - software, business services, India's share and targets
bullets: India is the world's 7th-largest services exporter. Its share of global services trade rose from 2% (2005) to 4.3% (2024) (ES 2025-26). IYB 2026, using WTO data, ranks India 8th with the same 4.3% share.
Services exports were USD 387.5 bn in 2024-25 (+13.6%) against imports of USD 198.7 bn, a steady surplus (IYB 2026).
In FY2025-26 services exports grew 15.3%. Software and business services made up 77.8% of them (APPCA, Jun 2026). CAGR was 14% over FY23-FY25, about double the pre-pandemic 7.6% (ES).
Earlier target (asked by APPSC): India's share of world services exports was to reach 4.2% by 2022. The government's overall export target is USD 1 trillion (LENS, Jul 2025).

bullets: The RBI (Amendment) Act, 2016 inserted Sections 45Z to 45ZO into the RBI Act, 1934 (APPCA). APPSC-GS 2022 key: amended in 2016.
MPC constituted under Section 45ZB; its decisions bind the RBI (LENS Dec 2025). First meeting October 2016 (TH 26 Mar 2026).

EBLR: from 1 Oct 2019, new floating-rate personal/retail and MSE loans must be linked to an external benchmark. Options: repo, 3-month or 6-month T-bill yield, or an FBIL-published rate (APP).

bullets: "Backward Classes" is not defined in the Constitution (APPSC G2 2017 key: the "defined" statement is the wrong one).

27% OBC quota in central jobs from 1993; in central educational institutions under the CEI (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006, in force Jan 2007 (IYB 2026 says 2007) after the 2005 amendment to Art. 15 (IYB) [GK for the Act's year].

Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006 (in force 2007): 27% OBC seats in central institutions (IYB; GS 2007 key: 93rd Amendment); OBC = classes "so determined by the Central Government" (APP).

sections.topic: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › National Commission for SCs (338), STs (338A) and Backward Classes (338B); Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (350B) › Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC
bullets: *Indra Sawhney v UoI* (16 Nov 1992) upheld 27% OBC reservation, introduced the creamy layer, and directed a permanent body for OBC-list inclusion/exclusion → NCBC Act, 1993 (in force 2 April 1993).
The 102nd Amendment also removed backward classes from the NCSC's purview .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-4 › Social stratification and mobility in India › Mobility through reservation, education, migration
bullets: Education: better education brings better jobs and higher social standing; the emerging class system allows upward mobility (APP).
Reservation: backward classes in the South (Self-Respect Movement of Periyar) demanded reservation in government jobs; reservation led to group mobility (APP).
Reservation has also broadened the urban middle class by bringing in backward classes and Dalits (APP).
Occupational mobility: e.g., Ezhavas of Kerala moved from toddy tapping into tailoring and cottage industries (APP).
Migration and urbanisation: city anonymity and caste-blind public spaces weaken caste identity, but migrants carry caste networks and prejudices into cities (APP).

bullets: Debate: NALSA (2014) asked governments to treat transgender persons as socially and educationally backward (a vertical OBC-type quota); the community seeks horizontal reservation cutting across SC/ST/OBC/General. The issue resurfaced in June 2023 with a Mumbai protest against Maharashtra's reply to the Bombay High Court (APPSC 2022).
Karnataka - first State to give 1% reservation to transgender persons in all government services (July 2021) (APPSC 2023).

items.title: NISD To Organise Five-Day Geriatric Care Training Programme In Diu Tomorrow
items.summary: Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, will inaugurate the training programme at Education Hub, Diu. He will also administer the Pledge for Welfare of Senior Citizens to the participants. Director NISD, Shri Gaurav Singh Rajawat, will be coordinating the inaugural session. The Collector, Diu, Shri Rahul Dev Boora, will formally welcome the dignitaries and participants.

facts.text: Around 50 Anganwadi Workers, frontline workers and grassroots-level functionaries are expected to participate in the programme, which is aimed at strengthening community-based support systems for senior citizens and enhancing the capacity of personnel engaged in last-mile service delivery.

The programme will also cover basic first aid and response to common emergencies, communication skills, psychosocial support, loneliness and social isolation, emotional well-being, and dementia awareness and basic caregiving approaches .

items.title: Rural Development Ministry holds national level rural training centres meet
items.summary: Secretary Rural Development calls for a modernising courses, AI-Enabled Digital Transformation, Improving credit linkages 08 OCT 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi A two-day National Level Review Meeting of Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETI) Stakeholders was organised by the Ministry of Rural Development at Shillong, Meghalaya.

facts.text: The meeting brought together senior officials of the Ministry, State Governments, State Rural Livelihood Missions (SRLMs), sponsoring banks, NAR and RSETI functionaries from across the country to review physical and financial progress at the mid-point of the financial year and chart a strategy fo…

Noting the programme's national footprint of 647 RSETIs covering 634 districts since its inception in January 2009, the Secretary said around 64 lakh persons have been trained, about 72% settled, but the satisfying fact is that 46 lakhs of women in about 72% of total trained beneficiaries.

Describing RSETI as one of the country's longest-running and most successful skill development programmes, and a 100% centrally sponsored one, he highlighted its growing role as a convergence platform for training under various Government schemes.

Bank wise presentations were also made by the respective bankers, while State wise presentations were jointly delivered by the State Directors/State Controllers of RSETIs and the National Officers of SRLMs.

items.summary: Sivakumar, Member Secretary, Central Silk Board, other senior officials and heads of various organizations under the Ministry of Textiles. Established under the North-East Region Textile Promotion Scheme (NERTPS), the state-of-the-art facility has an annual capacity to produce 30 lakh Disease-Free Layings (DFLs) of mulberry hybrid seed and preserve up to 1 crore DFLs.

facts.text: Established under the North-East Region Textile Promotion Scheme (NERTPS), the state-of-the-art facility has an annual capacity to produce 30 lakh Disease-Free Layings (DFLs) of mulberry hybrid seed and preserve up to 1 crore DFLs.

The upgraded facility is expected to further strengthen the regional sericulture value chain, generate employment opportunities, and create business opportunities for local suppliers and traders, thereby contributing to the socio-economic development of sericulture farmers.

He underlined the sector’s significant livelihood potential, with sericulture estimated to generate employment for around 29.50 lakh persons during 2025-26, highlighting the region’s strong potential in Vanya silk production and its growing importance in India’s silk economy.

bullets: 1950: Position Fundamental Right under Art. 19(1)(f) (acquire, hold, dispose of property) and Art. 31 (no deprivation save by authority of law; acquisition only for public purpose with compensation)
44th Amendment, 1978: Position Deleted Art. 19(1)(f) and Art. 31 from Part III; made it a legal (constitutional) right under Art. 300A, Part XII, Chapter IV

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › Election Commission of India - composition, appointment (2023 Act), powers and functions › Disputes regarding election - EC vs courts, Article 329 bar
bullets: Art. 329(a): laws on delimitation and allotment of seats cannot be questioned in court; Art. 329(b): an election can be challenged only by an election petition .

By convention courts do not interfere once the poll process begins; the ECI cannot review a result. Petitions go to the High Court (Parliament, state legislatures) and the Supreme Court for President/VP (Art. 71) (UPSC).

Art. 329(b): an election to Parliament or a state legislature can be questioned only by an election petition under the RPA 1951. Such petitions are tried by the High Court, with appeal to the Supreme Court .
President/VP election disputes: decided by the Supreme Court (Art. 71) .
The ECI does not try election petitions. It decides party and symbol disputes and advises on disqualification.

bullets: Also called the Prayaga-prashasti; a Sanskrit eulogy of Samudragupta's conquests (APPSC-GS 2025 key) composed by his court poet Harisena, in mixed prose and verse (champu style) .
Harisena held several posts at once: Kumaramatya, Sandhivigrahika and Mahadandanayaka (CDI, UPSC notes).
Do not confuse him with the later Jain author Harisena of the Brihatkatha Kosha listed in CDX - a different person .
The same pillar also carries Ashoka's edicts, the Queen's edict (queen Karuvaki ) and Jahangir's inscription (UPSC Art & Culture).
It glorifies war, in contrast to Ashoka's message of peace on the same pillar.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-6 › Important policies and programmes of the Government of Andhra Pradesh - welfare and social security › Health welfare - Dr NTR Vaidya Seva/Aarogyasri, 104/108, Family Physician
bullets: New insurance model announced May 2025 by Health Minister Y. Satya Kumar Yadav: cover up to ₹25 lakh per family per year for about 1.65 crore poor and middle-class families (APPSC PYQs).

108 emergency service: 768 ambulances, 9.22 lakh patients transported (APSES 2024-25); 108 and Aarogyasri are YSR-era schemes (TH, 9 Jul 2026). 104: mobile medical units giving fixed-day village health services .

Model change: under the Universal Health Policy, every citizen gets free treatment up to ₹2.5 lakh (insurance mode), and the poor get treatment up to ₹25 lakh through the NTR Vaidya Seva Trust (TH, 1 Mar 2026). The G2-GS 2024 statement that the new insurance model covers up to ₹25 lakh per family a year was keyed correct.
EHS (Employees Health Scheme): cashless treatment for State government employees and pensioners through the same Trust .
Health budget 2026-27: ₹19,305 crore (TH, 1 Mar 2026); AP MMR 45, IMR 24 (APSES).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-6 › Important flagship programmes of the Central Government - social sector (health, education, nutrition, housing) › ESI and EPF - establishments covered, wage ceiling, contribution rates, benefits
bullets: EPF: 12% of wages from employee and employer (10% for notified establishments) (LENSD, 4 Jul 2026). Covers establishments with 20+ employees .

EPF Scheme, 2026 replaced the EPF Scheme 1952 under the Code on Social Security. Members carry over automatically; voluntary contributions above the ceiling are allowed; the principal employer is liable for contract workers' PF; linking Aadhaar, PAN and UAN is mandatory (LENSD, 4 Jul 2026).

Wage ceiling for mandatory EPFO coverage raised from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 a month (Cabinet, LENSD 17 Sep 2026). The ₹15,000 ceiling dated from Sep 2014; the change is expected to add 51 lakh+ employees. Benefits: PF, EPS pension, EDLI insurance.

ESI (ESI Act 1948): ceiling ₹21,000 a month; employer 3.25%, employee 0.75%; medical, sickness, maternity, disablement and dependants' benefits . Under the SS Code, ESIC coverage is pan-India (CDI); SPREE (Jul 2025-Jan 2026) added 1.03 crore employees (TH, 17 Jan 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-4 › Impact of LPG on administration - downsizing, contractualisation, New Public Management › Contractualisation and outsourcing - contract employees in government, APCOS
bullets: Contract labour was 40.7% of the manufacturing workforce in 2022-23, up from 20% (1999) (Annual Survey of Industries). Contract-labour-intensive firms show 31% lower productivity (LENS Aug 2025).
About 8,000 outsourced APSRTC employees are paid through contractors; they face irregularities in wages, PF and ESI and demand equal pay (TH, 28 Jul 2026).
At NEDCAP, staff recruited after 1987 were kept only as contract or outsourced workers (TH, 29 Jan 2026).
